summary: No weekend arXiv batch was posted. From the latest Friday announcement, the strongest uncovered heavy-ion result is a four-dimensional lattice-informed QCD equation of state with a constructed critical surface; a three-fluid friction study provides a useful but non-equilibrium effective-viscosity diagnostic. PTagent offers an auditable LLM-to-deterministic-backend workflow, while Jianmu-Q warrants caution because its broad framing rests on small benchmarks.
strongest_paper_summary: A four-dimensional lattice-informed QCD equation of state with a critical surface, tempered by unquantified high-density truncation uncertainty.

papers.title: Four-dimensional QCD equation of state with a critical surface from contours of constant entropy density
papers.abstract: A lattice-informed equation of state in (T, muB, muQ, muS) is constructed through constant-entropy-density contour extrapolations, yielding a critical surface and explicit heavy-ion observables.

papers.title: Effective shear viscosity from the friction term in relativistic multi-fluid hydrodynamics
papers.short_authors: C. Spieles and M. Bleicher (2 authors)
papers.abstract: A three-fluid model maps friction-induced stress anisotropy onto an effective eta/s over BES/FAIR energies, with cross-section and grid-sensitivity tests.

papers.title: PTagent: An LLM-assisted tool for finite-temperature model construction in cosmological phase transitions
papers.abstract: An LLM agent assembles an auditable model specification while deterministic backends generate and validate numerical potentials after human approval.

cautions.title: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
cautions.abstract: A multi-agent workflow builds quantum-simulation pipelines for three small field-theory benchmarks and validates them against classical solvers, with selected hardware tests.
